dialogue.message: I want a local-first media production and review workbench. It should help me import video, audio, or assets, organize material, find review-worthy moments, generate reviewable results, and export reports and a package. I may connect local AI later, but do not use cloud services or pretend AI is already real.
CGKN asks about local-first expectations, privacy, acceptable degraded AI behavior, install difficulty, visual proof, and report/export evidence.
Keep it local, make it easy to run, do not depend on cloud AI, and show what evidence was actually produced.
CGKN compares candidate requirements and explains why a local media operations workbench is the strongest MVP direction.
I do not want a tiny clip demo, but I also do not want a fake full AI suite. Freeze a useful first version.
CGKN selects `Local video material processing workbench` and rejects less useful directions.
CGKN freezes MVP scope, non-goals, and acceptance criteria before implementation evidence is treated as success.
I accept this scope if you are explicit about what is degraded and do not sell fixture ASR as production AI.
CGKN writes product brief, technical plan, interaction design, and acceptance matrix tied to the selected requirement.
CGKN generates a shared local pipeline with orchestrator, stages, CLI, GUI, stage artifacts, schemas, and upstream/downstream traceability.
CGKN produces README, TEST_REPORT, DELIVERY_NOTES, screenshot evidence, smoke logs, delivery manifest, capability manifest, and final zip.
I opened the README to check the run command, package contents, and known limits.
This is not just a demo, right?
I checked whether there is a real final_project_bundle.zip and not only internal reports.
Has it really been run locally?
I inspected requirement decision docs, product contract docs, stage artifacts, capability manifest, and delivery manifest.
Which capabilities are real, and which are placeholder, fixture, or contract-only?
Is this real AI, or are transcription and ASR still degraded?
CGKN states ASR status `asr_contract_fixture_verified`, evidence tier `contract_fixture`, transcription `placeholder_transcription`, and commercial_ready remains false.
If I give this to my team, what is still missing?
Please make the README and delivery notes clearer about degraded mode, the ASR evidence tier, what is inside the zip, and the exact command that was actually run.
CGKN updates customer-facing README/DELIVERY_NOTES evidence and repackages through the local packager; the customer agent does not edit CGKN code or generated project files.
I retested by reviewing the updated README, delivery notes, manifest, smoke log, screenshot, and zip package.
Why can this not be called commercial ready yet?
I need a direct answer: can I sell this or roll it out to my team as production software today?
CGKN reports `NEEDS_REWORK` and commercial_ready `False` because production ASR, reliability runs, human review, and release operations are not complete.
I can accept the scoped local-first delivery only if the final score and evidence checks pass; that does not mean commercial readiness.
The independent scorecard computes the customer score from requirement, product, implementation, delivery, rework, degraded honesty, and commercial readiness separation.
The independent gap report lists remaining gaps without letting the customer agent change code or fabricate artifacts.

commercial_readiness.why_not_commercial_ready: COMMERCIAL_READY evidence is incomplete; candidate or delivery success alone is insufficient.

selected_requirement.customer_goal: I want a local-first media production and review workbench for individual creators or small teams. It can import video, audio, and asset files, organize a material library, define a processing workflow, generate clip or item analysis, flag candidate content worth reviewing, choose outputs, export a project package, and generate a processing report. It cannot depend on cloud services and must not pretend to have real AI models. CGKN should decide the real requirement, MVP scope, non-goals, acceptance criteria, and generate a runnable local project.
selected_requirement.interpreted_need: A local-first workbench for ingesting video, extracting or simulating audio, chunking/transcribing, analyzing segments, selecting clips, and exporting reviewable artifacts.
selected_requirement.target_user: Creators or operators who need repeatable local media processing.
selected_requirement.core_problem: Raw media work becomes untraceable and hard to evaluate when it is reduced to a single preview.
selected_requirement.selected_product_shape: Desktop/web GUI plus CLI over a shared orchestration core.
why_this_requirement: It turns the rough video-tool goal into a concrete local product with testable artifacts.
It has enough value, clarity, delivery feasibility, testability, MVP boundaries, and risk control for a first build.
why_not_other_requirements: single_static_page_demo_requirement: customer_value_score_lt_50, clarity_score_lt_50, small_demo_for_complex_goal, demo_degradation_risk_high, fake_pass_risk_high
non_goals: Guaranteed real speech recognition without configured model
selected_requirement.acceptance_summary: A run creates stage artifacts, GUI/CLI share the same core, and missing models are reported as degraded instead of success.
known_assumptions: The selected MVP can be revised if the customer rejects the chosen direction.
open_questions_not_blocking: Confirm exact runtime platform and preferred UI style before final polish.

commercial_readiness.reason: COMMERCIAL_READY evidence is incomplete; candidate or delivery success alone is insufficient.

next_recommended_action: Collect representative production media/ASR runs, approved human review evidence, and reliability evidence before any COMMERCIAL_READY claim.
